'''Paul O'Brien ''' (22 January 1954 – 16 October 2018<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=O’BRIEN, Prof. Paul | id = U59835 | volume = 2016 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref>) was professor of [[Inorganic compound|Inorganic Materials]] at the [[University of Manchester]],<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=23103639300}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|zfmka2wAAAAJ}}</ref> where he served as head of the [[School of Chemistry, University of Manchester|School of Chemistry]] from 2004 to 2009 and head of the [[School of Materials, University of Manchester|School of Materials]] from 2011 to 2015. He died on 16 October 2018 at the age of 64.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/rsc/paul-obrien-former-vice-president-of-royal-society-of-chemistry-dies-aged-64/3009649.article|title=Paul O'Brien, former vice president of Royal Society of Chemistry, dies aged 64|date=19 October 2018|access-date=23 October 2018}}</ref>

==Education==
O'Brien was educated at [[Cardinal Langley Roman Catholic High School|Cardinal Langley Grammar School]] in [[Middleton, Greater Manchester]] and the [[University of Liverpool]] where he was awarded a Bachelor of Science degree in 1975.<ref name=whoswhoB>{{Who's Who | title=O'BRIEN, Prof. Paul | id = U59835 | volume = 2016 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> He went on to complete a PhD degree at [[Cardiff University|University College, Cardiff]] in 1978<ref name=whoswho/> with a thesis on the [[catalysis]] of the [[racemisation]] of [[amino acid]]s supervised by Robert D. Gillard.<ref name=pophd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Paul|last=O'Brien |title=Catalysis of the racemization of amino acids |publisher=University of Wales |year=1978 |oclc=896125568|id={{ProQuest|301320104}}}} {{subscription required}}</ref>

==Research==
O'Brien was an inorganic materials scientist focusing on developing new chemical processes for manufacturing [[thin film]]s and [[nanoparticle]]s.<ref name=scopus/><ref name=googlescholar/><ref name="TrindadeO'Brien2001">{{cite journal|last1=Trindade|first1=Tito|last2=O'Brien|first2=Paul|last3=Pickett|first3=Nigel L.|title=Nanocrystalline Semiconductors: Synthesis, Properties, and Perspectives|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=13|issue=11|year=2001|pages=3843–3858|issn=0897-4756|doi=10.1021/cm000843p|hdl=10773/5962|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref name="GovenderBoyle2004">{{cite journal|last1=Govender|first1=Kuveshni|last2=Boyle|first2=David S.|last3=Kenway|first3=Peter B.|last4=O'Brien|first4=Paul|title=Understanding the factors that govern the deposition and morphology of thin films of ZnO from aqueous solution|journal=J. Mater. Chem.|volume=14|issue=16|year=2004|pages=2575–2591|issn=0959-9428|doi=10.1039/B404784B}}</ref><ref name="TrindadeO'Brien1997">{{cite journal|last1=Trindade|first1=Tito|last2=O'Brien|first2=Paul|last3=Zhang|first3=Xiao-mei|title=Synthesis of CdS and CdSe Nanocrystallites Using a Novel Single-Molecule Precursors Approach|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=9|issue=2|year=1997|pages=523–530|issn=0897-4756|doi=10.1021/cm960363r|hdl=10773/5787|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Amongst these are [[Chemical vapor deposition|chemical vapour deposition]] techniques for [[Chemical compound|compounds]] containing [[sulphur]] or [[selenium]], and a very simple method for making [[quantum dot]]s – [[semiconductor]] nanocrystals that show [[Quantum mechanics|quantum behaviour]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|author=Anon|year=2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117102905/https://royalsociety.org/people/paulobrien12015/|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/paulobrien12015/|archive-date=2015-11-17|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor Paul O'Brien FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |date=25 September 2015 |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies }}}}</ref>

He collaborated on projects with physicists, computer scientists and electronic and electrical engineers. His interest in the toxicity of metal [[ion]]s led to collaborations and publications with toxicologists, pharmacists and clinicians.<ref name=frs/> He was an advocate of communicating science to a wider audience and gave popular talks – usually on nanotechnology – including [[Café Scientifique]] and school lectures. He edited several books, including a series on [[nanotechnology]] for the [[Royal Society of Chemistry|Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC)]].<ref name=frs/>

In 2001, he founded the [[University spin-off|spin-off company]], [[Nanoco|NanoCo Technologies]], to commercialise the manufacture of quantum dots not containing heavy metals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/news-events/articles/2018/oct/paul-obrien-tribute|title=Paying tribute to Paul O'Brien|last=Chemistry|first=The Royal Society of|date=2018-10-18|website=www.rsc.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-30}}</ref>

O'Brien was passionate about international development and over two decades he worked tirelessly to encourage excellence in teaching and learning across Africa, with very strong ties to the [[University of Zululand]].<ref name=":0" /> His efforts changed the lives of many young African scientists and his students called him their “Father of Chemistry”.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iom3.org/fellows-lounge/feature/2018/nov/13/obituary-professor-paul-obrien-freng-frs-ceng-fimmm|title=Obituary - Professor Paul O'Brien FRS FREng CEng FIMMM {{!}} IOM3|last=Lewis|first=David J|website=www.iom3.org|access-date=2019-07-01}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
O'Brien's awards include the Kroll Award, the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining| Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining (IOM3)'s]] Sir [[Colin Humphreys]] Award (for outreach) and Platinum Medal, the [[Society of Dyers and Colourists|Society of Dyers and Colourists (SDC)]] Gold Medal, the RSC's first [[Peter Day (chemist)|Peter Day Award]], and honorary degrees from the [[University of Zululand]], the [[University of Liverpool]] and the [[University of Aveiro]]. O'Brien was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2013|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2013]]; his certificate of election reads: {{centred pull quote|Paul O'Brien is distinguished for his many original contributions to chemistry and [[materials science]], notably in the use of novel molecularly defined precursors from which to prepare important functional electronic or optical materials in well-defined forms. Processes he pioneered have been widely adopted. His discoveries include substantial improvements in the constitution, [[stoichiometry]] and nature of [[Precursor (chemistry)|precursors]]. He has shown how relatively stable compounds can be used to prepare high quality functional materials, and developed improved methods to convert precursors into useful functional products, devising and refining ways by which [[nanoparticle]]s syntheses can be controlled within the size limits require for device use<ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC%2F2013%2F26%27) |title=Certificate of election EC/2013/26: Paul O'Brien |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |author=Anon |year=2013 |archive-date=10 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510082310/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC%2F2013%2F26%27) |location=London |access-date=30 May 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

In 2016, O'Brien was appointed a [[Order of the British Empire|Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (CBE)]] in the [[2016 New Year Honours]] for services to science and engineering,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wilmslow.co.uk/news/article/12933/new-years-honours-for-stalwart-fundraiser-professor-and-ex-footballer|title=New Years Honours for stalwart fundraiser, professor and ex-footballer - wilmslow.co.uk|website=www.wilmslow.co.uk|access-date=2019-07-01}}</ref> received the [[Longstaff Prize|RSC Longstaff Prize]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/magazine/features/a-tale-of-two-continents/|title=A tale of two continents {{!}} The University of Manchester Magazine|last=Chilton|first=Alexander|website=The University of Manchester|access-date=2019-07-01}}</ref> and was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/news/news-releases/2016/september/academy-elects-top-engineers-as-fellows-at-its-40t|title=Academy elects top engineers as Fellows at its 40th anniversary AGM|date=2016-09-09|website=Royal Academy of Engineering|access-date=1 July 2019|archive-date=15 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115190524/https://www.raeng.org.uk/news/news-releases/2016/september/academy-elects-top-engineers-as-fellows-at-its-40t|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was elected as a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/O'Brien_Paul|title=Academia Europaea: Paul O'Brien |access-date=8 November 2023}}</ref>
